label: rem:q-beta-direction-sanity-gate
title: $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ precision-ladder $\S 4(d)$ formalize-first gate — any candidate Habiro element $F(q_0)$ must have magnitude consistent with the target observable's order of magnitude; the $z(q_0) \approx 0.6127 < 1$ direction obstruction is the canonical refutation precedent
html:
Any candidate Habiro element F(q) must satisfy the direction-sanity invariant: |F(q_0)| must be in the same order of magnitude as the target ratio \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{CODATA}} / [Q_A(q_0) \cdot \cos(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q_0))]. A candidate predicting a magnitude differing by more than 10\times is screened out.

This is a magnitude check applied before any wide numerical search. This is an order-of-magnitude screen, not a structural exclusion: no proved invariant forbids a candidate outside the window, so a screened-out candidate is not refuted. The target is \approx 1 on the retired z = 1 base and \approx 1.76 on the canonical z = q^3/(q^2+1) base.

The screen is the predicate \mathrm{Scr}_{10}(t,|F(q_0)|) of The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), with the threshold 10 (one decade each way) a convention and the target t a comparison value. Everything provable about the gate is in that proposition. In particular a larger threshold only admits more candidates (item 1); a screen-out implies F\ne F_{\mathrm{true}} only if the true kernel passes the screen (item 2), which is a comparison with data; and the obstruction behind the canonical precedent, a candidate of the form B\,z(q_0)^m with 0\le z(q_0)\le1, needs no threshold (item 4): if B<t then B\,z(q_0)^m<t for every m. Whether B<t holds is again a comparison with data, and it fails on the retired z=1 base, where t<1. The additive band |m-t|\le10t, an alternative form of the gate, is not this window: on nonnegative magnitudes it is the one-sided bound m\le11t, so it rejects no too-small candidate (item 6).
